content.value_statement: Library build setup can be slow and hard to configure across formats, declarations, and frameworks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical tsdown guidance for reliable builds.
actual_capabilities: Explains tsdown installation, Node.js runtime requirements, and first build commands.
Creates tsdown configuration for ESM, CJS, IIFE, UMD, and declaration output.
Guides React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, WASM, CSS, and executable build recipes.
Helps migrate common tsup options to tsdown patterns.
Covers hooks, plugins, programmatic builds, watch mode, workspaces, and CLI flags.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run or verify builds by itself.
It assumes users can install development dependencies and use Node.js 22.18 or newer.
Advanced framework plugins may require separate package documentation.
Release automation examples need project-specific review before use.

use_cases.title: Set Up Library Builds
use_cases.description: Create a tsdown setup for TypeScript packages with multiple output formats and declarations.

use_cases.title: Bundle Component Libraries
use_cases.description: Configure framework-specific builds for React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, CSS, and peer dependencies.

use_cases.title: Migrate From tsup
use_cases.description: Map existing tsup options to tsdown defaults, output behavior, and migration checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Build Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a TypeScript package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up tsdown for my TypeScript library. I need ESM and CJS output, declaration files, and a clean output folder.

prompt_templates.title: Add Framework Library Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure tsdown for my React component library. Keep React external, generate types, and explain the package scripts I need.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate From tsup
prompt_templates.scenario: Move an existing package to tsdown.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing tsup setup and plan a tsdown migration. Preserve output formats, declarations, targets, externals, and package scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Design Monorepo Release Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tsdown build strategy for a monorepo. Include watch mode, declarations, package exports, dependency externalization, and CI validation.

output_examples.input: Set up an ESM and CJS build for a TypeScript library.
output: Recommends Node.js 22.18 or newer for the build environment.
Adds entry points, output formats, declaration generation, and clean output.
Suggests package scripts and a verification build step.

output_examples.input: Migrate my React component package from tsup.
output: Maps tsup options to tsdown equivalents and default changes.
Keeps React and React DOM external to avoid duplicate framework copies.
Calls out migration checks for declarations, targets, and package exports.

output_examples.input: Optimize watch mode in a monorepo.
output: Uses workspace filtering to limit rebuild scope.
Recommends ignoring generated, test, and dependency folders.
Separates fast local watch settings from stricter CI validation.

best_practices: Generate declaration files for TypeScript libraries unless the package intentionally ships source only.
Externalize peer dependencies such as React, Vue, and Solid to avoid duplicate framework copies.
Test built output on every Node.js version declared in package metadata.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle secrets or private environment values into browser output.
Do not copy release automation examples without reviewing publish permissions.
Do not use root output directories or broad clean patterns in shared repositories.

faq.question: Does this skill run tsdown for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration guidance and command examples for an agent or developer to apply.

faq.question: What Node.js version does tsdown need?
faq.answer: The skill documents Node.js 22.18 or newer for running tsdown at build time.

faq.question: Can it help with type declarations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains declaration generation, sourcemaps, Vue support, and related TypeScript settings.

faq.question: Does it support framework libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, CSS, and WASM library builds.

faq.question: Can it migrate a tsup project?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers key option differences, default changes, and migration checklist items.

faq.question: Should I use the release automation examples directly?
faq.answer: Review them first. Commands that clean files or publish packages need project-specific safeguards.
